speakers: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host, Top Traders Unplugged; transcript spells 'Neil Castro Lson')
Eric Crittenden (founder, Standpoint, managed futures plus equities mutual fund; transcript spells 'Critan')
Andrew Beer (managed futures ETF manager, DBi)
summary:
Systematic Investor Ep.404 (mid-June 2026): trend followers Eric Crittenden and Andrew Beer on managed futures ETFs, the trend-plus-equities combination, and why allocators fail at trend.
Themes: behavioral reasons investors abandon trend, simple blunt rules beat complex ones out of sample, correlation-based optimization hurts, indices understate larger managers, sustainable Sharpe ratios are low for single strategies.
Trend profits come from early, contrarian-looking entries enforced by algorithmic discipline; blend it with other assets.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: is a fertile soil environment for finding trends and uh there's a lot of dislocation, a lot of uncertainty and I think a lot of risk premiums to collect going forward
claims.claim: Dislocation and uncertainty in mid-2026 create fertile ground for trends and risk premia to collect.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: the tariff um tant tantrums that was going on in April of last year. Since then, it's basically been smooth sailing.
claims.claim: April 2025 tariff tantrums caused a hard drawdown for trend followers, followed by 12-14 months of many trends and risk premia.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: when I see the valuations of AI companies and the kind of circular financing and everything that's going on in it
claims.claim: Beer is skeptical of AI company valuations and circular financing, while recognizing the real optimism and wealth creation.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my trend barometer finished yesterday at 43. That indicates a slightly weaker environment
claims.claim: A trend barometer at 43 indicated a slightly weaker trend environment in June 2026, with equities and metals most challenging.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: Stocken CTA index down 58 basis points but still up 9.83 for the year
claims.claim: June 2026 data: SG CTA +9.83% YTD, SG Trend +9.49%, Short-Term Traders +4.84%, versus MSCI World about +8%, S&P 500 +8.6% and global aggregate bonds +0.64%.
claims.indicator: SG CTA, SG Trend, SG Short-Term Traders indices

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: market makers are starting to um build the infrastructure such that a portfolio like ours would run smoothly and efficiently in an ETF structure
claims.claim: Diversified international futures portfolios could not run in an ETF because market makers lacked liquidity infrastructure, but this is changing.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: you don't need all of these markets. We don't need to be trading platinum and Japan and you know, Malaysian palm oil and whatnot.
claims.claim: Niche markets (platinum, Japan, palm oil) are nice-to-haves; performance attribution shows they do not matter much, so reducing dimensionality for an ETF costs little.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: the newest generations of advisors a lot of them are ETF only
claims.claim: Many new advisors and individual investors are ETF-only, so an ETF wrapper widens distribution; tax benefit is mainly on the equity sleeve.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the more complicated the underlying is, the more illquid the underlying is, the more the more risk they have of moving the price of the underlying
claims.claim: ETF market makers hedge via the underlying, so ETFs on deep, liquid instruments trade within a penny or two of NAV, while illiquid underlyings widen spreads.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you have an ETF desk and the ETF desk will basically do block trades or trade in dark pools or things like that
claims.claim: Large model allocators trade ETFs through ETF desks via blocks or dark pools; ease of moving large dollars is a selling point.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: We need a third leg of the asset allocation stool and how do we build that?
claims.claim: A $4bn single-day inflow into BlackRock's new multi-strategy ETF shows trillions in model portfolios seeking a third leg of the asset allocation stool, which will eclipse mutual fund assets.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: about as statistically obvious as anything that managed futures as a strategy plus equities um is you know 1 plus 1 equals three or four
claims.claim: Combining managed futures with equities is statistically about as obvious as it gets (1+1=3 or 4), with offerings from Fidelity/Crochet, ManHL, Hoffstein, JP Morgan, Winton and Aspect.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: They tend to uh buy things that are up a lot and sell them as soon as they stall out.
claims.claim: Allocators buy what is up and sell when it stalls, which makes it hard for them to hold uncorrelated strategies.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: a $10 gain gives you one unit of pleasure but a $10 loss gives you two units of pain
claims.claim: Under prospect theory, benchmark-relative loss aversion (S&P 500 or 60/40) made it nearly impossible to keep allocators in managed futures beyond a few quarters, even though adding it improves everything.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: returns go up, V goes down, draw downs get smaller, everything gets better
claims.claim: Adding a decent managed futures program to any portfolio raises returns, lowers volatility and reduces drawdowns.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: I'm not afraid to own equities as long as I've got the long convexity trend component that can fill those potholes during the hard times or at least the expectation of that
claims.claim: Owning a large equity position is comfortable when paired with a long-convexity trend component that fills drawdowns.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: to get that benefit that we're talking about where you a diversifier that actually increases returns and lowers risk at the same time, you're not going to fit into any one of those boxes nicely
claims.claim: A diversifier that raises return and lowers risk does not fit style boxes (large cap growth, fixed income active), complicating distribution.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: I strive for equal risk contribution from the equities and from the trend side.
claims.claim: Size equity and trend sleeves for equal volatility contribution (e.g. 100% of an 8% vol managed futures program plus 50% of 16% vol stocks) because the better performer is unknown.
claims.direction: equal vol weights equities and trend

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: aggressive enough to be competitive, but not so aggressive that, you know, we're going to be scrambling in um, riskoff events
claims.claim: Choose the volatility level that is competitive but survivable: double risk invites VaR and compliance stress, half risks lagging inflation and fees.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the average hedge fund mutual fund has been a catastrophe for investors like 2 to 3% peranom returns after 200 basis points in fees
claims.claim: Average hedge fund mutual funds earned only 2-3% a year after about 200bp fees, worse than random, reflecting marketing-driven product development.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: Normal product development in the mutual fund and ETF business is marketing and distribution people
claims.claim: Most products are built by distribution teams chasing flows with no ownership over five years, unlike managers building for their own capital.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: Stock and bond correlations break down. bonds break down as a diversifier started in in 2022
claims.claim: Since 2022 bonds stopped diversifying stocks, so ETF model allocators with only stocks and bonds look for a 3-5% alternative allocation.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: their their their actions often don't follow their words
claims.claim: Advisors say they want diversification or tail protection but often do not act on products that deliver it.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: that's a success from a diversification perspective, I'm going to be blamed for it, but if I got 50% equity in there as well and I'm up 70, no one's going to complain
claims.claim: Allocators fear being blamed when equities double and their diversifier gains only 20%; blending trend with 50% equity avoids that regret.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: they don't want to sell a penny
claims.claim: Capital-efficiency-focused allocators do not want to sell stocks, which drives demand for full portable-alpha (100% equity plus overlay) products.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the difference between what it means when you invest with a manager where they are really committed and invested in the product and in a product that is just one of a hundred
claims.claim: Due diligence should weigh whether the manager has a large share of net worth in the product versus a product that is one of many at a big asset manager.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it's largely a one-sided option
claims.claim: Large firms launch trend products as a one-sided option (market if it works, close if not), so allocators must vet the team's modelling credibility over 5-10 years.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: the simple ones are the ones that hold up on data they haven't already seen
claims.claim: Complex trend programs look better in hindsight and in presentations, but simple durable rules hold up much better out of sample.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: those were simple, blunt tools that put us on the right side of risk premium
claims.claim: In April 2020 simple trend rules kept the fund short crude oil when prices went negative, showing blunt tools handle unprecedented events.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: the majority of the returns that trend followers collect can be mapped back to you know four, five, maybe six principal components
claims.claim: Most trend follower returns map to 4-6 principal components (energies, fixed income, grains, USD), about 90/10 Pareto, so adding many markets adds little.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: you make a lot less money. Uh, and you fool yourself into thinking you have less risk than you really do
claims.claim: Overweighting uncorrelated markets via correlation, cointegration or copula optimization reduced profit and understated risk in live trading.
claims.testable: yes - compare equal weight vs optimized

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: in trend following you make your money in market environments where the ball's going up, the correlation's going up
claims.claim: Trend profits arrive when volatility and correlations rise; low-vol, low-correlation periods bring whipsaws and few profits.
claims.direction: press risk when vol and correlation rise
claims.conditions: low-vol gentle correlation periods are whipsaw

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: this simple like super ultra simple trend following model that he built which is basically looking back over a year and reflexively just buying it
claims.claim: Crochet's ultra simple 12-month lookback trend model had a Sharpe of about 1 at 12.5% vol; to resemble CTA universe returns, about 800bp had to be removed.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: You're not shown the 37 models that were thrown out that didn't make it into the final paper.
claims.claim: Published research hides discarded models, so readers only see the final results (selection bias).

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: are you making it from 70 instruments working in your favor or are there clusters of instruments because oil's going up and it's dragging the whole energy complex with it
claims.claim: Trend profits may come from clusters (energy, metals, equities) moving together rather than 70 independent instruments.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: because the short-term models are getting people out at, you know, 9:31 before the markets move, not at the end of the day, uh, or the risk controls are kicking in
claims.claim: Possible reasons for CTA Sharpe ratios far below a simple model's: short-term models exit before moves, and risk controls cut positions.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: you get all the blowups in the index right because they're all usually the biggest managers then they blow up so that drags the index down
claims.claim: CTA indices include the biggest managers and their blowups, but omit smaller managers who do well, so may understate best-in-class trend; institutions also pay lower fees than those embedded in the index.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: I don't see some secret pool of large high sharp ratio managers except in very very limited circumstances
claims.claim: No hidden pool of large, high-Sharpe trend managers exists; efficiency among large managers means a simple replication gets competitive rank.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they're not simple in any way, shape, or form, and they trade hundreds of markets
claims.claim: ISAM, which is complex and trades hundreds of markets, has been hardest to beat, a counterexample to simplicity being better.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: we know alpha is lumpy but but but your alpha was ultra super lumpy in a in in a very very compelling way
claims.claim: Trend alpha is lumpy: Dunn's very large 2022 gain carried its numbers for a decade.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: You get out to 10, no one has a sharp ratio over one.
claims.claim: Plotting Sharpe ratios of hedge funds against track record length shows the maximum falls with length: none over 1 at 10 years and about 0.65 at 15-20 years.
claims.indicator: Sharpe ratio vs track record length

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: single strategies good ones have a sharp ratio somewhere between 3 and 04 sustainably
claims.claim: A good single strategy sustains a Sharpe ratio of about 0.3-0.4.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: if you combine strategies, you take a point4 from equities and you take a point4 from managed futures, you know, you get something like 1.1
claims.claim: Combining 0.4-Sharpe strategies (equities, managed futures, tail hedging) gives a combined Sharpe of 1.1-1.2, sustainability uncertain but closer to 1 than any single strategy.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: how what else is drawing down when you're drawing down
claims.claim: A Man Group paper ('Don't look down') argues what matters for drawdowns is what else is drawing down at the same time.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: when the space makes money, it's it's it's not trend following. It's not getting into something late, right?
claims.claim: Reframing CTA as 'contrarian tactical alpha': money is made by early, uncomfortable entries, not by joining crowded trends late.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: buying gold at 2200 after it's been dead money for a decade
claims.claim: Trend wins came from early contrarian-looking trades: crude oil in January after declines, gold at 2200 after a decade of nothing, shorting Treasuries in September 2020 at 70bp.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: This is the this this isn't a strategy. It's an asset class. It's an asset class that by its nature is dynamic and tactical.
claims.claim: Managed futures is a dynamic, tactical asset class whereas other portfolio assets are static betas; because of low correlation all returns show up as alpha.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: the algorithmic discipline to get into trends before they're socially and politically uh safe is crucially important
claims.claim: Algorithmic discipline forced uncomfortable positions (short equities in 2002 and 2008, short energy before COVID, long cocoa up 400%) that produced alpha.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: in the trend following world, 50 60 sometimes 70% of your trades don't work out
claims.claim: 50-70% of trend trades lose, so keep losses small and hold winners for years.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: at one point I was short natural gas I think for eight consecutive years
claims.claim: Trend rules stayed short natural gas for eight years in a heavy contango market, capturing persistent roll-down.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: algorithmic discipline forced you to not waste your time on it for 20 years and to be long and strong ever since then
claims.claim: Gold was dead money for two decades; trend rules ignored it, then went long after the breakout and held for 25 years.

claims.speaker: Eric Crittenden
claims.quote: on a day-to-day basis it tends to drive people crazy which is why I blend it with other assets
claims.claim: Trend is hard to live with day to day, so blending it with other assets in a multi-asset product helps investors stay invested.
